Start slow and use a metronome. They make free metronome apps for your cell phone - and you can get one that ticks, tocks, and blinks a flashing light.

Don't try to play at-speed. Start slow and speed will come. Never, ever rush the speed aspect. Guitar is mostly muscle memory. Once you learn it, it's easier to pick up speed. Trying to pick up speed to fast will give you bad habits that you have to unlearn in order to get better. If you skip developing them, you'll get better more quickly and will have the ability to go even further.

When I have given lessons, correcting bad habits has taken up a lot of my time and effort. Don't rush it. Play it as slow as you need to play it in order to play it right.

But...

You're going to way to play it slow BUT consistent. If you can do a certain section faster, don't. Play that at the same speed and tempo that you play the rest of the song.

You can also practice the basic chord shapes. E A D G C, Amin Emin, and a B# and Fmin go a long ways. Learning to transition between them smoothly and rapidly will help.

When you get those done, learn the barre and the grand barre - and that'll give your fingers a bunch of exercises you can work out and learn with.
